refactor: restructure wayland home-manager modules

Splits the monolithic hyprland config and flat sway module into a
layered, per-compositor structure with shared common tooling.

## Structure
- wayland/common.nix: shared wayland tools activated via
  robot-disco.wayland.enable (rofi, mako, cliphist, brightnessctl,
  wireplumber, util-linux, wallpaper)
- wayland/wallpaper.nix: extracted shared wpaperd config
- wayland/hyprland/: hyprland.nix + lock-screen.nix (hypridle/hyprlock)
- wayland/sway/: sway.nix + lock-screen.nix (swayidle/swaylock)

## Key decisions
- Both WMs auto-enable robot-disco.wayland.enable; lock-screen modules
  are intentionally NOT auto-enabled since sway and hyprland coexist
  and only one idle daemon should run at a time
- System-provided binaries (hyprctl, swaymsg, uwsm) use bare commands;
  home-manager packages use store paths in service/daemon configs
- Pin uwsm in hyprland exec-once to store path as it is system-provided

## Also includes
- NixOS wayland module reorganization (laptop/desktop/wayland.nix)
- darwinSystem/nixosSystem: pass through extraModules
- Document package reference conventions in CLAUDE.md

Events are propogated in a more central way.

Unit tests revealed that I needed a smarter way to handle how to process events via streams.
I wound up having a central game stream that the Game class emits to, rather than my original idea of having every monster/player emit directly (eases some management and removes some coupling.) I'm anticipating that this stream will have to be carved into more selective ones which various UI subsystems (and potentially other objects!) will respond to.
